title: Partial types
hook: partial splits one type across files so a generator can own a slice and you can own the rest. C# 14 extends that idea to partial constructors and partial events.

sections.heading: Partial classes and methods
sections.prose: partial class (and struct, interface, record) means every part shares the same type identity. Source generators emit one part; you write another. Partial methods used to be void, private, and erasable if unimplemented. Later C# versions allow richer partial methods with implementations required. Use partial to keep generated CSV mapping or protobuf stubs out of your git-owned logic — not as a substitute for composition.

sections.heading: C# 14: partial constructors and events
sections.prose: C# 14 lets instance constructors and events be partial. There is exactly one defining declaration and one implementing declaration. Only the implementing constructor may have this() or base(). Only one part may declare a primary constructor. A partial event’s defining part looks field-like; the implementing part supplies add and remove. That is how a generator can declare the surface and your file can wire RabbitMQ subscription add/remove without colliding.

snippets.label: Partial type with C# 14 constructor split
snippets.explanation: The generated file declares the constructor. Your file implements it. One primary constructor across all parts is the C# 14 rule.

sections.heading: file-local plus partial
sections.prose: Generators often combine file types (previous access-modifiers topic) with partial public types. Consumers see one public worker; helpers stay file-local. Events as a programming model (delegates, add/remove, extension members) wait for module 10. You only need to know here that the declaration can be split.

interviewTakeaways: partial is one type, multiple files — the generator pattern.
C# 14: partial constructors and partial events, one implementer each.
Only one part may use primary constructor syntax.
commonPitfalls: Two primary constructors in different parts.
Putting business logic in the generated file so the next generate wipes it.

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS interface merging is a type-space feature. C# partial is one runtime type built from several syntactic parts.
JS classes are one declaration (or a runtime mixin). Splitting implementation is modules and composition, not a language-level partial type.
